text: Who were the Baro-Bhuyans in Bengal history? They were a shifting confederacy of regional landed-military leaders who resisted Mughal expansion, especially in Bhati.
Why is the Baro-Bhuyans phase important? It explains why Mughal incorporation in Bengal was prolonged, negotiated, and shaped by riverine resistance.
How did Bhati geography matter? River channels, marshland routes, and fortified river nodes enabled asymmetric defense against larger imperial forces.
